title: Behaviour
description: What a business does with the structure one domain describes: the roles it expects, its Actions, the Operations that say which role performs them on what, the workflows that sequence those Operations, the policies that decide them, and the defaults for what no policy governs. It names its domain and never changes it, so a business can be modelled structure first and given behaviour later. A set holds at most one behaviour document per domain. Its home is its domain: its policies and defaults target the domain or an entity in it.

dna.description: The behaviour vocabulary this document is written in.

id.description: Kebab-case. Unique among the documents of a set.

domain.description: The structure domain this document describes.

uses.description: Other behaviour documents whose Actions this one refers to.

roles.description: The kinds of actor this domain expects, such as an underwriter, a credit bureau or a scheduler. A role is the same in every organization that uses the domain; the organization says who fills it. Ids are unique. An Action's actors, an Operation's actor, a role performer and a role condition name a role by its id here, or as domain/role for a role of a domain whose behaviour document this one uses.

policies.description: The domain's policies. A policy with no target applies to the whole domain; a target names the domain or an entity in it, never another domain. Organization and workspace policies belong to their access documents.

defaults.description: The decision for a request no policy governs, declared at the domain or at an entity in it. The effective default of a request is the one declared at the deepest target that contains it; where the domain declares none, the workspace's applies.

role.description: A kind of actor the domain expects. It has no records: people, agents, automations and outside firms fill it.

id.description: Kebab-case. Unique among the roles of its behaviour document.

default.description: A default and the target it is declared at.

target.description: A domain or an entity address, relative to the workspace, as a policy's target. Omitted, it is the document's home.

default.description: deny: what no policy governs is refused, so only what is allowed proceeds. allow: what no policy governs proceeds, so all proceeds except what is denied. A policy reference that does not resolve denies under both.
